loop.direction: south straight eastbound, north straight westbound (counter-clockwise from above)
loop.carrier: 850 x 440 mm at 700 mm pitch (FORTNA option 2)
loop.speed_note: owner cap 2.0 m/s: 0.2 m per frame at 10 fps, well under one 0.7 m carrier pitch, so a tracker never has to guess which carrier a parcel jumped to between frames

conveyors.note: D02's boom joins here and runs north into the feed corner (line A layout b)

machines.chute_layout_note: Chutes on ONE side of the loop (north straight) is a deliberate simplification. Real cross-belt loops usually have chutes on both sides, often on two levels. One side keeps the plan readable, puts every chute in one camera row (2 cameras instead of ~4) and keeps one bagging aisle. Spoor's logic does not depend on it.

weigh_section.why: an in-motion scale reads no barcode and emits no event of its own; the DWS controller tracks the parcel by photo-eye and merges weight + dims into the single tunnel event at SP-TUNNEL (ScanEvent.weight_g / dims_mm)
weigh_section.still_filmed: yes — see checks.weigh_section_filmed; the photo-eye merge can pin the wrong weight on parcels running too close together, and video is how you prove that

assumptions.why: pack assumption; small enough for ~18 cameras; real Malaysian hubs are 6–10x bigger

assumptions.value: 12 m bays along X; interior column line at Y = 25 m (spans 25 m + 15 m)
assumptions.why: owner-approved pushback: keeps columns out of the sorter and chutes and gives camera mounts between bagging and staging
within the pack's 10–12 m (a Shah Alam shed lists 12 m clear)

assumptions.value: 3.0 x 3.0 m, centres 4.0 m apart, dock height 1.2 m
assumptions.why: centre spacing within Blue Giant's 3.7–4.3 m; opening and dock height are assumptions; leveller plate covers lorry/trailer deck differences
owner-approved: chutes need enough drop (1.5 -> 1.0 m over 2 m) to slide convincingly

assumptions.value: straights 22 m, radius 4 m, length 69.1 m (~99 carriers at 0.7 m)
assumptions.why: radius per FORTNA minimum; length chosen for 12 chutes + reject on one side (Skynet Hounslow-style, chutes one side)

assumptions.value: 1.0 x 0.8 m, rim 0.9 m; chutes 1.3 m long, lip 1.0 m
assumptions.why: no published size found; sized so each chute lip sits 0.1 m above the rim over the bag mouth at a 19° slope (cardboard on steel slides from ~17°), leaving a 1.8 m bagging aisle before walkway W3

assumptions.value: 1.0 m wide at 1.5 m pitch; 2.8 m gap between C06 and C07
assumptions.why: width owner-approved (max parcel 1.0 x 0.7 x 0.7 m); pitch cut from 1.6 to 1.5 m so a crossover (XO-1) can land between C06 and C07 while C12 still clears the reject chute
height / yaw / tilt picked by a search over real mount points (column, drop-pole, wall bracket) to cover each camera's duty area at its PPM target, with occlusion — not guessed

assumptions.value: 1.2 m wide; deck 3.3 m over the loop, 2.4 m over the induction belt; stairs ~42°
assumptions.why: deck = carrier/belt height + 0.7 m max parcel + 0.2 m structure + clearance; industrial stairs stay at or under 45°

assumptions.value: 3 x 1.0 m push-bar doors (FE-1, FE-2 south; FE-3 east) + staff door
assumptions.why: positions per owner; egress distances NOT checked against Malaysian UBBL / Bomba rules — fictional hub, not a compliant design

assumptions.value: walkways 1.2 m; one forklift lane 3.0 m; 4 zebra crossings
assumptions.why: common warehouse practice, no Malaysian source; lane keeps >= 0.5 m from the loop guard
shortened so the forklift lane can pass between the office and the loop's east curve

assumptions.value: 3.0 m high around the NW store
assumptions.why: screen the deliberate blind corner; steel racking of folded sacks and nested empty cages is normal in hubs
the common 4 x 6 in thermal shipping-label size (industry standard, not a measured Malaysian figure)

seconds_per_frame.settings: EEVEE 2688 x 1520 (full resolution, owner rule), 8 samples, spot high-bays, shadows only from pools the camera sees within 22 m, 5 cm shadow texels, 2 shadow steps, max shadow pool, PNG write; ray tracing costs ~nothing here
